root_cause.text: In the xe DRM display init path, `xe->info.probe_display` was determined before `intel_display_device_info_runtime_init()`, so when display was later found absent/disabled by fuses the driver still executed suspend/shutdown display cleanup (`xe_display_flush_cleanup_work()` / `for_each_intel_crtc()`) against uninitialized or cleared mode config, causing a NULL pointer dereference.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves `intel_display_device_info_runtime_init(display)` earlier and adds `if (!intel_display_device_present(display)) { xe->info.probe_display = false; unset_display_features(xe); return 0; }`, while the CVE text says “the display may also be disabled via fuses, detected at a later time in `intel_display_device_info_runtime_init()`. In this case, the xe driver does `for_each_intel_crtc()` on uninitialized mode config in `xe_display_flush_cleanup_work()`, leading to a NULL pointer dereference.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a runtime display-presence check during early initialization and disable display probing and features when the display is unavailable.
intent_record.what: In `xe_display_init_early(struct xe_device *xe)`, a call to `intel_display_device_info_runtime_init(display);` was inserted immediately after `intel_display_driver_early_probe(display);`. A new runtime check was added using `intel_display_device_present(display)`, and if the display is not present, the code sets `xe->info.probe_display = false;`, calls `unset_display_features(xe);`, and returns `0` before continuing to `intel_opregion_setup(display);`.
intent_record.how: This change initializes display device information earlier and then conditionally aborts further display initialization when runtime probing determines the display is unavailable. As a result, it prevents the driver from proceeding with display setup and feature exposure on systems where display support has been disabled or is not present at runtime.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove an incorrect early device-info runtime initialization call from display startup so initialization occurs at the proper stage.
intent_record.what: The call to `intel_display_device_info_runtime_init(display);` was removed from `xe_display_init_early(struct xe_device *xe)`, leaving `intel_bw_init_hw(display);` followed directly by `intel_display_driver_probe_noirq(display);`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the early display initialization path no longer performs the device-info runtime initialization at this point, so that setup is deferred or handled elsewhere before the display driver probe continues.

Remove an incorrect early device-info runtime initialization call from display startup so initialization occurs at the proper stage.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it adds an early runtime check for display presence and disables display probing/features when display is absent, preventing later cleanup code from running against uninitialized mode config and avoiding the NULL dereference.

The change removes an early device-info runtime initialization call, which matches the root cause where probe_display was evaluated before runtime init and led to cleanup running on uninitialized/cleared display state. This directly addresses the initialization ordering bug behind the NULL dereference.

candidates.rationale: This early probe occurs before runtime display device info is initialized, so xe->info.probe_display can be set too early and later shutdown/suspend cleanup may run against an uninitialized or cleared display configuration when the display is actually absent.
This is part of the early display-init path executed before the runtime presence check, contributing to the driver proceeding as if display is available even when fuses later disable it.

Calling this at the wrong time is the core ordering bug: xe->info.probe_display was determined before runtime device-info initialization, leaving the display state stale and allowing cleanup paths to dereference invalid mode-config state.
This probe runs after the misplaced initialization ordering and can proceed with a stale probe_display decision, setting up later suspend/shutdown cleanup to touch uninitialized display structures.

vuln_statements.explanation: This call was made at the wrong point in startup: the display probe decision had already been made before runtime device-info initialization, so xe->info.probe_display could stay stale and later suspend/shutdown cleanup could dereference uninitialized or cleared mode-config state when display was actually absent.

This probe executed after the misplaced ordering, allowing the driver to continue with an incorrect display-presence decision. That stale state enabled later cleanup paths to run against invalid display structures and trigger the NULL pointer dereference.
